review: Jujur, kalau lewat Terminal Ferry Batam Centre ini emang kerasa banget vibe-nya sibuk. Namanya juga gerbang utama internasional, jadi jangan kaget kalau suasananya selalu hectic, apalagi pas akhir pekan atau jam-jam keberangkatan feri. Buat saya pribadi, nilai plusnya di sini adalah lokasinya yang sudah terintegrasi langsung dengan mal. Jadi, kalau nunggu keberangkatan, nggak mati gaya—tinggal nyeberang dikit udah bisa cari makan atau sekadar ngadem. Itu ngebantu banget sih buat kill time. Tapi ya, konsekuensinya harus siap mental sama antrean imigrasi yang kadang bisa panjang banget. Saran saya, jangan mepet kalau mau berangkat, harus kasih jeda waktu yang cukup biar nggak keteteran. Secara fasilitas, tempat ini tergolong fungsional—nggak yang mewah-mewah banget, tapi sudah cukup oke untuk kebutuhan mobilitas rutin. Overall, buat ukuran terminal sibuk, tempat ini lumayan bisa diandalkan asal kita paham manajemen waktunya

Batam Centre Fast Ferry Terminal cukup ramai karena menjadi salah satu pintu utama keluar masuk Batam, terutama untuk rute internasional seperti ke Singapura dan Johor. Lokasinya strategis, dekat dengan pusat kota dan beberapa pusat perbelanjaan. Area terminal cukup luas dan fasilitas dasar seperti tempat duduk, loket tiket, serta pemeriksaan imigrasi tersedia dengan baik. Namun saat jam sibuk antrean bisa cukup panjang dan suasana terasa padat. Secara keseluruhan terminal ini cukup memadai untuk perjalanan laut, meskipun kenyamanan bisa lebih ditingkatkan saat ramai.
Good service, fast, and effective. The toilet is clean, and the area is simple enough for first timer. Lihat terjemahan (Indonesia)

Pagi-Pagi ke sini untuk menyebrang ke spore. Pelabuhan Batam Center merupakan salah satu gerbang utama bagi wisatawan dan pebisnis yang ingin menyeberang ke Singapura dan Malaysia. Sebagai pelabuhan internasional yang sibuk, tempat ini dikenal dengan suasana yang tertib dan kondusif, memberikan kenyamanan bagi para penumpang yang akan berangkat maupun yang baru tiba. Salah satu hal yang paling mencolok di Pelabuhan Batam Center adalah sistem antrian dan pengelolaan penumpangnya yang teratur. Papan petunjuk arah tersedia dengan jelas, sehingga memudahkan pengunjung dalam mencari loket tiket, area imigrasi, dan ruang tunggu. Petugas di pelabuhan juga cukup sigap dalam membantu para penumpang, baik yang baru pertama kali datang maupun yang sudah sering bepergian. Kebersihan di area pelabuhan juga terjaga dengan baik. Fasilitas umum seperti toilet, ruang tunggu, dan area makan cukup bersih dan nyaman. Selain itu, suasana di dalam pelabuhan cenderung tertib, dengan kontrol keamanan yang ketat tetapi tetap efisien. Proses imigrasi berjalan cukup cepat, terutama jika penumpang sudah menyiapkan dokumen yang dibutuhkan. Dari segi aksesibilitas, Pelabuhan Batam Center terhubung langsung dengan pusat perbelanjaan, sehingga penumpang yang datang atau menunggu keberangkatan bisa berbelanja atau bersantap dengan nyaman. Tersedia pula berbagai moda transportasi, seperti taksi dan layanan transportasi online, yang memudahkan perjalanan ke berbagai wilayah di Batam. Secara keseluruhan, Pelabuhan Batam Center merupakan pelabuhan yang tertib, kondusif, dan memiliki fasilitas yang cukup baik. Bagi wisatawan maupun pelaku bisnis yang sering bepergian ke Singapura atau Malaysia, pelabuhan ini menjadi pilihan utama karena kepraktisan dan kenyamanan yang ditawarkannya.
Pelayanan tiket bagus, kemarin beli tiket ferry majestic. Sayang toiletnya kurang terawat

⭐ 1/5 — Worst Travel Experience Ever. Detained Without a Clear Reason. I have travelled extensively across Europe, Turkey and Southeast Asia, and I can confidently say that this was the worst travel experience I have ever had. My wife, our child and I travelled to Batam with friends for a simple weekend getaway. We cleared Malaysian Immigration, received our departure clearance and boarded the ferry without any issue. The moment we arrived at the Batam ferry terminal, a police officer approached us, took our passports and brought our family into a room. Later, our child was allowed to leave with our friends while my wife and I were kept there. We were made to wait for almost TWO HOURS with no proper explanation. Only after we repeatedly demanded answers were we told that we were being detained because the Malaysian police had supposedly requested it. That explanation made absolutely no sense. If Malaysian authorities had actually placed any restriction on us, how did we clear Malaysian Immigration and legally depart Malaysia without any problem? The whole situation ruined our trip. We no longer felt comfortable staying in Batam, so we choose to return to Malaysia immediately. Here is the most shocking part. When we arrived back in Malaysia, Malaysian Immigration interviewed us. We explained everything and asked what case or issue had caused us to be detained in Batam. They could not identify any reason for it. There appeared to be no case or immigration issue involving either of us. They were also puzzled as to why we had been detained after we had already cleared Malaysian Immigration normally. So I would genuinely like to know: Why were we detained for almost two hours? Why were we separated from our child without a clear explanation? Why were we told that Malaysian police had requested our detention when Malaysian authorities could not identify the reason for it? Being detained in a foreign country without being clearly told why, especially while travelling with your child, is not something any traveller should have to experience. What was supposed to be a relaxing weekend getaway turned into an extremely stressful and disturbing experience. I am sharing this so other travellers are aware of what happened to us, and I sincerely hope the relevant authorities investigate and provide a proper explanation. For us, this was completely unacceptable and easily the worst travel experience we have ever had. Lihat terjemahan (Indonesia)

CORRUPT IMMIGRATION OFFICERS AT THIS FERRY TERMINAL IMMIGRATION On 21 February, my family and I made a plan to visit Batam, Indonesia. The Chinese New Year holiday had just passed, and we wanted a short, peaceful getaway—two days of rest and sightseeing before my mother returns to the Philippines. It was meant to be simple family time. We are Philippine passport holders - husband, myself and my daughter have valid SG long term pass. Indonesians grant 30-day visa-free entry for Philippine passport holders. We had return tickets within the allowed period. We had hotel bookings. Everything was straightforward. But the moment we reached immigration in Batam on 21 Feb 2026, 1030AM Indonesian time, things changed. We were suddenly held back and questioned. The officers accused us of traveling to Batam “only to extend my mom’s visa in Singapore.” This accusation shocked us. Why would Indonesian immigration be concerned about Singapore’s ICA policies? We were entering Indonesia legally under Indonesia’s visa-free scheme. We were not overstaying anywhere. We were not violating any Indonesian law. Despite explaining that this was a short 2-day leisure trip, we were escorted into an office for further “interrogation.” The room was poorly lit and tense. There were other tourists inside as well, including an Indian passport holder who also appeared distressed. The atmosphere felt intimidating. Questions were repeated. The tone was accusatory, as if we had already done something wrong. Then the officer’s tone changed. He told us we had “two options”: 1. Change my mother’s flight and book her a ticket back to the Philippines on a date they wanted. 2. Pay SGD 150 as a “penalty” for “transiting” in Batam. Penalty for what violation? There was no clear explanation. No written notice. No official receipt mentioned upfront. No formal charge. Just two “options.” Why should Indonesian immigration dictate when my mother flies back to the Philippines? Why was there a “penalty” when we were within Indonesia’s visa-free entry rules? At that moment, fear took over. We were in a foreign immigration office. We saw how the officer spoke to other tourists. We did not know what could happen next—would they deny entry? Cancel our passports? Blacklist us? Create further complications for our travel? Feeling intimidated and powerless, and wanting to avoid further trouble, we agreed to pay the money. What was supposed to be a relaxing family trip turned into a deeply stressful and unsettling experience. It leaves travelers questioning: 1. Are short leisure trips now suspicious? 2. Is visiting Batam after staying in Singapore automatically treated as wrongdoing? 3. Why are tourists pressured with vague “penalties” without clear written violations? Experiences like this damage trust. Tourism thrives on safety, fairness, and transparency. When travelers feel intimidated or pressured without clear legal basis, it creates fear—not confidence. We came for rest and sightseeing. We left with disappointment. This will likely be our last visit to Batam. To fellow travelers: always keep your documents complete, know your visa rules, and stay calm—but also be aware of your rights. No holiday should begin with fear. Lihat terjemahan (Indonesia)

review: Batam Centre Point International Ferry Terminal - Functional But Basic Location: Batam Centre, Kota Batam, Kepulauan Riau Rating: ⭐⭐⭐ (3.5/5) I've passed through this terminal several times over the past year, so I've gotten pretty familiar with how it operates. The Good: The basics are covered well enough. There are plenty of SIM card kiosks right when you arrive, which is handy if you need to get connected immediately. Immigration processing is straightforward - nothing fancy, but it moves along at a reasonable pace. Luggage retrieval is simple and easy to navigate. The real bonus is the overhead walkway that connects directly to Mega City Mall. Makes getting to the Grab taxi stand super convenient - you don't have to deal with touts or figure out where to go. Just walk across and you're there. The Not-So-Good: It's a functional terminal, but that's about it. Don't expect much in terms of amenities or comfort while you're waiting. The facility feels pretty basic and could use some updating to make the arrival/departure experience more pleasant. Bottom Line: Does the job for getting in and out of Batam, and the connection to Mega City Mall is genuinely useful for onward travel. It's not going to wow you, but it won't give you major headaches either. If you're a regular traveler to Batam like me, you'll appreciate the straightforward layout even if it's nothing special. review: Hey guys, it’s your favorite elite traveler back with another unfiltered review—and this time, we need to talk about the gatekeeping situation at the Batam Center Ferry Terminal. As an Indonesian who travels extensively, I am usually so proud to welcome international visitors to our beautiful country. But my recent arrival at Batam Center at PM was, without exaggeration, an absolute NIGHTMARE. If this terminal is meant to be a major international gateway, the current reality is a total embarrassment to our national hospitality. Here is the raw truth about what you can expect if you land here late at night: 1. The Immigration Bottle-Neck (The Absolute Worst Part) Imagine an entire ferry of exhausted travelers arriving at PM, only to find exactly one immigration officer working the counter. The inefficiency was mind-boggling. But the real vibe-killer was the officer handling the desk—an older woman named Ibu May. To say she was rude is an understatement. Unprofessional, highly inefficient, and frankly, throwing what I can only describe as a 5-year-old’s tantrum behind the desk. As an Indonesian, it broke my heart to watch her. She is single-handedly ruining the image of Indonesian hospitality for every international tourist standing in that excruciatingly long line. 2. Zero Digital Readiness Before you even get to the chaos inside, there is no coordination at the entrance. There are no QR codes shared or displayed at the entrance for required digital arrivals or health forms before you enter the terminal. Everyone is left scrambling in the dark, trying to figure out what they need to do. It’s clunky, outdated, and unacceptable for a major transit hub in 2026. 3. The Transport Monopoly Trap Once you finally escape the terminal, don't even think about opening your Grab or Gojek apps. The terminal strictly bans ride-hailing apps to protect their local taxi monopoly. Normally, I’m all for supporting local drivers, but the execution here is a safety and logistical hazard. Most of the drivers stationed there are very elderly, struggle to understand directions, and—unbelievably—do not know how to type into or use Google Maps to reach your destination. If you don't know the exact streets yourself, you are essentially stranded with a driver who can't navigate. The Verdict 🚨 Batam Center Ferry Terminal needs a massive wake-up call, urgent staff retraining, and a complete tech overhaul. To the management: please address the lack of personnel, the attitude of staff like Ibu May, and let ride-hailing apps in so travelers can actually get home safely. We went to Batam as a group of 3 couples over the Vesak Day weekend (29 to 31/5/2026) and chose Harbour Bay terminal since it's the nearest to I-hotel Nagoya. We arrived on 29/5 around 3pm (Indo time) & auto-gate was down. Quite a number of visitors had to be transferred to the manual queue, it was quite messy with no proper management of the queues for entry. Luckily the service was quite fast & efficient. On 31/5, we started to head towards the departure area at 4.45pm to queue for the 5.30pm slot departure to Singapore. Although alot of passengers were milling around the departure hall - a normal sight for weekends - but the system was initially still organised & well-controlled as a staff was stationed at the start of the queue to ensure only passengers for the earliest departing ferry entered the queue. Announcements were also made both in Bahasa & English. However, the situation took a different turn after 5pm when the staff left his post unattended and the announcement for 5.30pm departure was announced together with the 5.15pm departure within a span of less than 5 minutes. Things got worse at the passport-scanning station. I was among the 1st 10-15 visitors queuing at the manual lane since there was a long queue at the auto gate. 1 of the lady officers attending to manual scanning suddenly stood & left her desk to tell us that Singapore passport-holders to queue at the auto-gate. I believe they could have managed this better by stationing officer at the queue entrance instead of directing the ones who are already in the front row to go back and join the auto-gate queue at the back. Do remember that this group consisted of passengers from 2 different vessels and there was already a congestion at the auto-gate queue due to the close interval between the 2 announcements earlier. Harbour Bay ferry terminal used to be smooth & less chaotic..please ensure there are sufficient officers/staff stationed at strategic points/locations in the departure area to manage the crowds. Tips: Sebaiknya datang ke pelabuhan lebih awal, terutama saat peak season, untuk menghindari antrian panjang. Pastikan Anda memiliki tiket yang valid sebelum memasuki kapal. Membawa kartu brizzi yang sudah terisi saldo Ikuti instruksi dari petugas pelabuhan untuk memastikan kelancaran proses bongkar muat kendaraan.

Catatan untuk naik roro (membawa kendaraan) dari punggur-ke tanjung uban melalui pelabuhan telaga punggur : 1. Untuk membeli tiket, siapkan uang dalam bentuk e-money (kartu brizzi). Bila tidak punya kartu, dapat membeli di konter yang telah disediakan (didekat gerbang masuk kendaraaan) 2. Di konter tersebut, anda juga bisa mengisi ulang kartu tersebut. 3. Selalu ingat/ memfoto plat kendaraan (karena dibutuhkan untuk syarat pembelian tiket) 4. Selalu membawa surat penting kendaraan (sim, stnk, dll) 5. Tidak membuang boarding pass (setelah pembelian tiket anda akan dapat 2/3 kertas dan salah satunya ialah kertas boarding pass yang merupakan syarat masuk kapal) 6. Setelah membeli tiket anda dapat mengantri/ membawa kendaraan ke tempat tunggu. 7. Berhati-hati saat masuk kapal.

Kejadian kemarin saat saya hendak pulang dari Batam ke Selat Panjang melalui Pelabuhan Sekupang. Saat tiba di pelabuhan, saya menuju konter yang jelas-jelas bertuliskan “Dumai Line” untuk membeli tiket. Setelah membayar dan menerima tiket, saya heran karena tiket yang diberikan ternyata bertuliskan “Batam Jet”. Saya kemudian bertanya kepada petugas, “Kok Batam Jet? Saya mau naik Dumai Line.” Namun petugas tidak menjawab pertanyaan saya dan hanya mengatakan, “Kapal besar.” Saya kembali menegaskan bahwa saya ingin tiket Dumai Line, tetapi petugas hanya diam. Lalu petugas lain mengatakan bahwa uang tidak bisa ditransfer kembali karena pembayaran sudah dilakukan. Untungnya akhirnya uang saya dikembalikan secara tunai. Setelah itu saya membeli tiket di konter Dumai Line yang sebenarnya, yang berada tepat di sampingnya, dan mendapatkan tiket yang sesuai. Yang membuat saya semakin kesal, ternyata orang tua saya pernah mengalami kejadian serupa. Karena tidak terlalu mengenal tulisan, mereka baru mengetahui tiket yang dibeli bukan Dumai Line saat sudah hendak naik kapal dan diberitahu oleh petugas. Saya sebenarnya tidak berniat memposting hal ini. Namun karena kejadian yang sama juga dialami oleh orang tua saya, saya merasa perlu menyampaikan keluhan ini. Mohon kepada pihak Pelabuhan Sekupang untuk menindaklanjuti dan mengawasi praktik seperti ini agar tidak ada lagi penumpang yang mengalami kebingungan atau dirugikan, terutama orang tua dan penumpang yang kurang memahami perbedaan loket maupun nama operator kapal. Terima kasih.

Terminal Feri Sekupang merupakan salah satu pelabuhan utama di Kota Batam yang melayani transportasi laut domestik dan internasional. Terletak di kawasan Sekupang, pelabuhan ini terbagi menjadi dua bagian, yaitu terminal domestik dan terminal internasional. Terminal domestik melayani rute antarpulau seperti ke Karimun, Tanjung Balai, Dumai, dan pulau-pulau di wilayah Riau , sementara terminal internasional melayani rute cepat ke Singapura dan Malaysia dengan waktu tempuh sekitar 45 menit. Fasilitas di Terminal Feri Sekupang tergolong lengkap dan modern. Di dalamnya tersedia ruang tunggu berpendingin udara, loket tiket yang tertata rapi, area makan dan kafe, layanan money changer, ATM, serta musholla. Tersedia juga layanan transportasi darat seperti taksi resmi dan parkir kendaraan yang luas. Terminal internasionalnya bahkan dilengkapi dengan business lounge, Wi-Fi gratis, serta sistem imigrasi yang cepat dan efisien, menjadikannya alternatif favorit bagi penumpang yang ingin menghindari keramaian di pelabuhan Batam Centre. Selain fungsi utamanya sebagai pelabuhan penumpang, Terminal Feri Sekupang juga menjadi wajah kota Batam bagi wisatawan mancanegara. I work in Singapore and I took my kids and in-laws(Visit pass holders) to Batam as it was a long weekend. It was a bitter experience where my family including 2 kids(2 and 6yo) were held inside a room with no proper reason for nearly 2 hours. We waited for 15 mins clueless and realized the supposed to be officer started eating his lunch, smoking and laughing with other workers without any sense that there were older people and small kids inside that small suffocating room and I actually felt that they are obliged to attend to us first or atleast give an explanation. After all, we were not there for any free service. I stepped out because of smoke and they demanded us to stay in. We were treated no less than criminals and were literally ill treated. After an hour a guy came in and finally, I understood that they presumed that we were there for Visa extension. I was asked why we didn’t go to Malaysia, after all it was my choice to do whatever I wish and it is never mentioned anywhere in the immigration guidelines. They asked for 100$ to let us go after 1.5 hours. I asked them the passports back so that we can return, which they never did. Later, head of the immigration came, got our passports stamped and got our money back and apologised. I felt they were so racist and had some cold attitude to people from India. I will never go back again. Totally hate it, forget being an educated officer, these people are so insane that they should learn how to treat fellow human beings. Lihat terjemahan (Indonesia)
